card.name: "No known treatment" statements
card.fires_on: The word "for" or the following punctuation in phrases like "there is no known/effective treatment for [condition]", where the text says nothing can be done about a condition.

modes.label: After "no known treatment"
modes.description: The word "for" right after "no known treatment" in a sentence about an established adverse condition.
modes.example: There is no known treatment<< for>> established cases of tardive dyskines

modes.label: After the condition is named
modes.description: A comma or semicolon right after the condition named in a "no treatment" statement, before a qualifying clause.
modes.example: Currently, there is no effective treatment for chondrolysis<<;>> patients who have experienced chond

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning "can only" or "cannot" (Chinese 只能, 无法, and English cannot), which fit a statement of inability or limitation.
card.plain: It fires when a label says there is no known treatment for a condition, as if a "cannot be treated" idea is coming.
